item.lead:
The module's first shared configuration is a plain table: a tuple of small records, each holding a name, a default value and a line of help text. Each record is a named tuple, so you read its parts by name instead of by position.

Look at how one record is built, then at a few entries: a page size of 100 and a query time limit of 1000 milliseconds. Then see how a loop reads every default.

perform.line:
/code Write a Python example that mirrors a settings table built from named tuples and prints each default.
Use these sizes and values: a namedtuple called Setting with fields name, default and help; a tuple SETTINGS with entries default_page_size = 100 ("Default page size for the table view"), max_returned_rows = 1000 ("Maximum rows that can be returned from a table or custom query"), num_sql_threads = 3 ("Number of threads in the thread pool for executing SQLite queries"), sql_time_limit_ms = 1000 ("Time limit for a SQL query in milliseconds"), facet_time_limit_ms = 200 ("Time limit for calculating a requested facet"). Standard library and numpy only; nothing imported from the source.
One comment per step, in the words the reader already knows: named tuple, table, default, help text.
Do not print or state any output.
